string-array.item: Make the first step small enough to finish today.

Turn the goal into one concrete action.
Finish a version, then refine it.
Reserve some uninterrupted time for this.
Start with the part you can verify most easily.
Name the help you actually need.
Clear the desk, then sort your thoughts.
Add a checkpoint to your plan.
Divide the challenge into three smaller questions.
Choose a step that makes tomorrow easier.
Turn one worry into something you can check.
Update the plan with real feedback.
Make room for what matters first.
Give yourself a chance to practice properly.
Put the idea into a simple prototype.
Agree on boundaries before working together.
You can begin while it is still imperfect.
A small stretch of progress counts today.
Pause. The answer need not arrive right away.
Have a glass of water, then return to it.
Rest your body; your thoughts need room too.
Sleep on it before making the judgment.
Not answering yet is also a choice.
Leave yourself a little quiet time.
Set aside what you cannot do just now.
Not every message needs an instant reply.
Give the feeling some time to settle.
Care for the parts of yourself you can care for now.
A pause does not make the whole effort a failure.
Remove one task from today.
Let the plan make room for your energy.
Look away from the screen for a moment.
A slower pace can reveal the path underfoot.
Empty space gives things room to breathe.
Quiet the inner hurry for a while.
Bring your attention back to one breath.
You need not solve everything while tired.
Let the question rest on paper for a while.
How would you understand this if it happened to a friend?
Separate facts, guesses and wishes.
Ask again: whose expectation is this?
Give the opposite choice one fair reason.
You can hold two possibilities at once.
Try replacing must with I choose.
Consider the longer effect as well as the present feeling.
There may be a question behind the question.
Not every difference needs a winner.
Describe it before judging it.
Look for the resources already available to you.
Separate the outcome from your worth.

Ask whether a third approach exists.
Admitting uncertainty leaves room to learn.
Return to the part you can influence.
One choice need not define your whole life.
Revisit the purpose and remove an unnecessary demand.
Let the answer be a beginning, not an order.
